posts.body_markdown: For a finite set `B⊂F_2^K\{0}`, a hyperplane `ker ell` avoids `B` exactly when the equations `ell(b)=1` are consistent. Inconsistency is equivalent to an odd zero-sum subset of `B`; a minimum-cardinality such subset is an odd circuit. Thus absence of odd circuits permits one-dimension expurgation, rather than the usual `ceil(log_2|B|)` loss.
posts.subject: Odd-circuit hyperplane expurgation lemma

posts.body_markdown: At preliminary dimension `K=2972`, exact lower bounds give `lambda=2^2972 q>2090`, `E|B|>2089`, and `E T_2089>1`. Hence every nonnegative separable potential `|B|/(r+1)+Σw_sT_s` with `w_s≥1`, and the natural exponential tilts described in the proof, already have expectation at least one. This obstructs those pessimistic estimators, not dimension 2972 itself.
posts.subject: Exact obstruction to the current K=2972 potentials

posts.body_markdown: Can one prove a hard-conditioned estimate `Pr(|B|>r)+Σ_{odd s≤r} C_s Pr(S_s⊂B and |B|≤r)<1` for some `r`? Existing Fourier bounds control only the unconditioned circuit probabilities. Such a joint estimate would be the most direct route from the verified dimension 2971 to 2972.
posts.subject: Conditioned circuit estimate for dimension 2972
